messages.text:
At 10¢ the KBOX costs you about $24 a month in power, on an $800 unit. 22 TH/s means it's drawing for a full 3.125 BTC block every ten minutes, year after year, and you keep the machine.

First miner, or adding to a setup?

For a first miner, same money buys more at the 40T: $799 for 40 TH/s versus the KBOX's 22 for $800. Power's higher — about $47 a month at your 10¢ — but it's nearly double the draws at the block, and it's a quiet desktop tower you can actually learn on. Ships Nov 21, 2026.

Desk or garage?

$799 for the 40T, plus $40 flat shipping at its weight. Power's about $47 a month at 10¢.

If you meant how much it stacks in sats, say so and I'll run that figure for the 40T.

Honestly, at 40 TH/s it's a trickle — sats land small and steady in your own wallet, and at home power they come to less than the electricity. That's not why people buy it. You're buying a real shot at a 3.125 BTC block, every ten minutes, for years.

Want me to get you the exact sats-per-month figure at today's difficulty?

context.pop: At 10¢ the GekkoScience KBOX runs about $24 a month, at 16¢ about $38 — what do you pay for power?
